card.large.p: With more than 1,500 visible nodes the folders collapse. A collapsed folder opens on its own when an event arrives about something inside it (external ones too, if they are visible), and closes again if the network goes past about 1,950 nodes.
card.outside.p: Your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, skills or /tmp show up as satellites in a separate cluster, joined to an "outside the repo" hub.
card.panel.p: The side panel resizes by dragging its left edge (or with ←/→ when it has focus), between 280 and 720 px, and remembers its width. Its Tools section counts skills, MCP servers and tools, CLI programs and Claude's built-in tools.
card.stream.p: At the bottom left of the graph, the last 6 actions as short lines ("Editing src/api/user.ts"). A Pre and its Post share one line; each line fades after 8 s, hovering pauses it and a click opens the event in the detail drawer.
card.subagents.p: Events from a subagent carry agent_id. Each one gets its own hue and paints a halo around the nodes it touches, so you can see what each agent explores in parallel.
card.timeline.p: A third view next to 3D and 2D: one row per file in order of first touch, grouped by folder, with time on the X axis (long pauses shortened) and bands for prompt turns and subagents. It draws only what is on screen.
ch1.aside: The server answers an empty 204 as soon as it has the body, before processing it. Claude Code waits about 1 ms (with a 2 s cap) and never gets anything it could read as a decision.
ch1.caption: Claude Code's hooks and the disk watcher reach the same server, which stores every event and pushes it over WebSocket to the 3D network. It listens on 127.0.0.1:7777 by default; if that port is taken, start tries the next 20, shows the one it uses and writes it into the hooks.
ch1.p1: There are two sources of information. The main one is Claude Code's HTTP hooks: every time Claude decides to use a tool, and every time it finishes, Claude Code sends a POST with a JSON body that describes the action. The second is a file system watcher, which sees the disk changes no hook describes precisely, like an rm inside a Bash command.
ch1.p2: Both reach the same local server. There each report becomes a small event (action, phase, paths and, for a tool, which tool it was) that travels over WebSocket to the browser and is kept in a log for replay.
ch1.rDocs: Any file of the built docs; /i18n/* and /img/* too, for the pages' dictionaries and images
ch1.rHelp: The user guide (guide.html). 404 while the docs are not built (npm run build:docs)
ch1.rHook: Claude Code's hooks. Empty 204, sent before the payload is processed
ch1.rRoot: The web app: the 3D, 2D and Timeline views, the side panel and the live stream
ch1.rWs: The event stream: hello with the tree and the latest events, then every event live. Only from the server's own origin, plus NEURONS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
ch2.cDoctor: Checks Node, hooks, allowlists, proxies, the built web app and the built docs
ch2.cHelp: Commands with their options and examples
ch2.cInstall: Installs or removes the hooks by hand (cleanup after a crash)
ch2.cLang: Language of the CLI messages. Without it: NEURONS_LANG, then LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES or LANG, then English
ch2.cLs: Lists the running viewers: repo, port, URL, PID and start time
ch2.cOpen: Opens that repo's viewer in the browser
ch2.cStart: Starts the server, installs the hooks while it runs and opens the browser. Options: --port N, --strict-port, --no-open, --no-install, --no-bash-diff
ch2.cStop: Closes the viewer and waits up to 8 s. --all closes every viewer; --force kills one that did not close and does its cleanup
ch2.caption: The hooks exist only while start runs: they are written at startup into .claude/settings.local.json (and bashEditDiffEnabled into ~/.claude/settings.json), Claude Code picks them up live, also in a session that was already open, and Ctrl+C (or neu stop) removes them. The server uses port 7777 by default, or the next free one.
ch2.p: The hooks only exist while the viewer is open. If Claude Code had an HTTP hook pointing at a server that is down, every tool would print a red hook error. That is why start writes them when it starts and removes them when it closes. A Claude Code session that was already open picks them up live, with no restart (verified with Claude Code 2.1.288).
ch2.pre: # terminal 1 cd ~/my-repo && neu # terminal 2 (a session that is already open works too) cd ~/my-repo && claude # when you are done: Ctrl+C in terminal 1
ch3.aside: The payload of a Read carries the whole file content. The normalizer drops it: only paths and metadata reach the browser and the log.
ch3.caption: A Read of src/api/user.ts produces two reports, gets two empty 204s and leaves two pulses on the network; the file's text never leaves the server.
ch3.fCli: Bash: the programs it runs (git, npm, gh...), at most 8, skipping wrappers, variable assignments and builtins like cd
ch3.fCommand: Bash: the command, up to 2,000 characters. Heredoc bodies are cut, and when the command writes files or runs inline code (>, tee, sed -i, python -c...) its quoted literals become …
ch3.fDesc: Bash and Agent: Claude's own explanation (tool_input.description), up to 300 characters
ch3.fDur: Post and failure: how long the tool took and, on failure, the first line of the error (up to 200 characters)
ch3.fPattern: Searches: the grep/rg pattern, the find -name glob or the Glob/Grep pattern
ch3.fTool: Kind (builtin, mcp or skill), name and, for MCP, the server: mcp__github__search_code becomes server github, tool search_code
ch3.fieldsLead: Besides the action and the paths, a tool event says which tool it was and carries a few short details. The detail drawer, the Timeline and the Tools section of the panel show them. None of them is file content.
ch3.p: Every tool produces two reports: PreToolUse when Claude decided to use it and PostToolUse when it finished. On the network they show as two pulses: a faint one (intent) and a full one (done). The timings come from real sessions with Claude Code 2.1.285 on macOS (the phase 0 capture and the smoke test).
ch4.caption: Every change the watcher sees goes through two questions: if a hook already covers it, it is suppressed; if a Claude Bash was open, it is Claude's; otherwise it is external. A hook covers a path while an Edit or Write on it is in progress, or for 2 s after bashEditDiff, an Edit/Write or an rm/mv reported it.
ch4.h2: Was it Claude or was it you?
ch4.p1: There is no delete tool. Claude deletes and moves with Bash (rm, git mv), and the hook only carries the command text. To know who changed a file, the server opens a window for every Bash command, from its PreToolUse until it ends (PostToolUse, a failure or a denied permission, plus 600 ms of grace), and matches every disk change against those windows.
ch4.p2: If Claude Code has bashEditDiffEnabled on, the Bash PostToolUse already carries the exact list of created, deleted and modified files. Hook and watcher are deduplicated: whichever arrives first lights the change and the other does not repeat it.
ch5.caption: An event on src/api/user.ts lights the path from the root, one hop every 80 ms, and the file glows for about 3.5 s. In the app the color depends on the action (table below); here orange only marks the path.
ch5.p1: The tree comes from git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard: everything tracked plus anything new that is not ignored. Every folder and every file is a node, and every line joins a folder with what it contains. Whatever .gitignore ignores stays out. Outside git the disk is walked skipping node_modules, dist and build, and in both cases the scan stops at 50,000 files.
ch5.p2: When an event about src/api/user.ts arrives, the light runs along the path from the root, one hop every 80 ms, and the target node glows and fades in about 3.5 seconds. The links it crossed stay tinted in the action color and fade slowly: 5 s, or 7 s for edits, creations and deletes.
ch5.s.create: Write of a new file, bashEditDiff with created, an mv from outside the repo, or the watcher inside a Bash window
ch5.s.delete: rm through Bash, confirmed by bashEditDiff or by the watcher
ch5.s.edit: Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, Write on an existing file, files modified according to bashEditDiff, or the watcher inside a Bash window
ch5.s.mcp: Any mcp__<server>__<tool> tool, labeled server/tool. It lights a file when its input has a file_path or a path
ch5.s.search: find, grep, rg, git grep through Bash, and the Glob and Grep tools when the build has them (the native 2.1.285 build does not)
ch5.s.skill: The Skill tool. It has no path, so it lights no node: it shows in the feed, the live stream, the Timeline and the Tools section with the skill name
ch5.s.tool: Agent, WebFetch and any other tool; it lights a file when its input names one
ch6.after: If the process dies abruptly, neu uninstall <repo> undoes the install, and the next start cleans up whatever was left on its own. On Windows a signal ends the viewer without letting it clean up, so neu stop does that cleanup itself.
ch6.h2: What it touches on your machine
ch6.p: What start changes in the Claude configuration (settings.local.json and bashEditDiffEnabled) has a backup and is reverted on close; if nothing else changed, those files end up byte for byte identical. .git/info/exclude and .neurons/events.jsonl stay on purpose.
ch6.r1a: Adds 14 HTTP hooks to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/hook?src=neurons, with timeout: 2. Keeps the hooks you already had
ch6.r1b: Removes only its own entries. If the file did not exist, it deletes it
ch6.r2a: Turns on bashEditDiffEnabled if it was off. Leaves it alone with --no-bash-diff or --no-install, and does not create the file if it is missing or is not valid JSON. Honors $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
ch6.r2b: Puts it back to its previous value when the last viewer closes
ch6.r3a: Backup of settings.json and the record of the viewers that use bashEditDiffEnabled (mode 0600)
ch6.r3b: Deleted when the key is reverted
ch6.r4a: The events.jsonl log (appended to), the lock, the install manifest and the settings.local.json.bak backup
ch6.r4b: The log stays, for replay; the backup is deleted on uninstall
ch6.r5a: Adds /.claude/settings.local.json and /.neurons/ if git did not ignore them (on every start, also with --no-install)
ch6.r5b: Stays; it is not versioned and keeps git status quiet
ch6.r6a: Records the viewer (repo, port, URL, PID) so that neu ls, neu open and neu stop can find it. Honors $NEURONS_HOME

f1.desc: Claude Code reports every tool call to the local Neurons server with a POST /hook and gets an empty 204 back; a file system watcher reports disk changes to the same server, which normalizes each report, appends it to events.jsonl and sends it over WebSocket to the browser, where the 3D network of the repository lights up.
f1.s1a: You type a prompt in the terminal
f1.s1b: Claude Code gets the prompt and picks tools
f1.s2: Claude Code tells the server with POST /hook
f1.s3: The server answers an empty 204 right away
f1.s4a: Claude Code reads and writes files in your repository
f1.s4b: The watcher sees disk changes and passes them to the server
f1.s5: The server normalizes the report and appends it to events.jsonl
f1.s6: The browser gets the event over WebSocket and the network lights up
f1.title: Neurons at a glance
f2.desc: Sequence diagram: neu start scans the repo, starts the server, writes 14 HTTP hooks into settings.local.json and opens the browser; then you open claude (or keep a session that was already open), which picks up those hooks and during the session sends a POST /hook for every tool, gets an empty 204 and the event reaches the browser over WebSocket; on Ctrl+C the CLI removes the hooks and reverts what it changed in the Claude configuration.
f2.s1: You run neu start in a terminal
f2.s2: The CLI takes the lock, scans the tree with git ls-files and starts the server and the watcher
f2.s3: It writes 14 HTTP hooks into settings.local.json and turns on bashEditDiffEnabled
f2.s4: It opens the browser, which gets hello with the tree when it connects
f2.s5a: You open claude in the same repo, or keep a session that was already open
f2.s5b: Claude Code picks up the hooks when the session starts, or live if it was already open
f2.s6: During the session every tool sends POST /hook, gets an empty 204 and the event travels over WebSocket to the browser
f2.s7: You close the viewer with Ctrl+C
f2.s8: It removes its hooks, restores the original bytes and reverts bashEditDiffEnabled
f2.title: What happens when you run neu start
f3.desc: Sequence diagram of a Read of src/api/user.ts: Claude Code sends PreToolUse and then PostToolUse to the server, which answers an empty 204 right away; the normalizer turns each payload into a VizEvent and drops the file content, and the browser receives over WebSocket first a faint intent pulse and then a full pulse with the light going from the root to the file.
f3.s1: Claude Code sends PreToolUse for Read src/api/user.ts to the server with POST /hook
f3.s2a: The server answers 204 with an empty body before processing anything
f3.s2b: The server hands the payload to the normalizer
f3.s3a: The normalizer returns a read pre VizEvent, with no content
f3.s3b: The event reaches the browser over WebSocket in 0 to 5 ms and the file gives a faint intent pulse
f3.s4a: PostToolUse arrives 4 to 7 ms later, with the whole file in the tool response
f3.s5a: The payload reaches the normalizer with the whole file
f3.s5b: The normalizer drops the file content: only the path and the action remain
f3.s6a: The normalizer returns a read post VizEvent
f3.s6b: Read post arrives over WebSocket: full pulse and light from the root to src/api/user.ts
f3.title: One Read, end to end
f4.desc: Decision diagram that classifies every disk change the watcher sees: if a hook already covers it (an Edit or Write in progress, or a report less than 2 seconds old), it is suppressed and only updates the tree; if not, and a Bash window is open, it is attributed to Claude with its session and agent; if there is no window, it is marked external in dim gray and can be hidden.
f4.s1: The watcher sees a change on disk
f4.s2a: First question: does a hook already cover that change, because an Edit or Write is in progress or because a hook reported it less than 2 seconds ago?
f4.s2b: If yes, SUPPRESSED: the event is not repeated, only the tree is updated
f4.s3a: Second question: was a Bash window open when the watcher saw the change?
f4.s3b: A window runs from the Bash PreToolUse to its PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure or PermissionDenied; Stop, SessionEnd or the next prompt also close it; always with 600 ms of grace, and it expires after 10 minutes
f4.s4: If there was a window, ATTRIBUTED to Claude, with that window's session and agent; an rm shows as a red delete
f4.s5: If there was no window, EXTERNAL: it was you or another program; it shows in dim gray and can be hidden
f4.title: Was it Claude or was it you?
f5.desc: Tree of a sample repository where a read event on src/api/user.ts lights the path root, src, api and user.ts with one hop every 80 ms, and the target file glows with a pulse that fades in 3.5 seconds.
f5.s1: A read event in the post phase arrives for src/api/user.ts
f5.s2: The light hops from the root to src, at t+0 ms
f5.s3: The light hops from src to api, at 80 ms
f5.s4: The light hops from api to user.ts, at 160 ms
f5.s5: user.ts glows with a pulse that fades in 3.5 seconds
f5.title: From tree to network: one lit path

page.subtitle: Neurons is a terminal command (neu). It starts a server on your machine, asks Claude Code to report everything it does and draws your repository as a network of nodes that lights up live. This page shows how the pieces fit together.
